description_en: The fountain is located to the western end of Koligāũ, under the main track.The monument is almost completely cemented. Only two water spouts with makara heads are preserved. Other architectural elements are either covered by cement or have been taken away to be re-used.Similar fountains, locally referred to asmugrāhā, are found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019). This monument can be roughly dated to the 14th-15th century, a period corresponding to the rise of the Rāskoṭī dynasty (14th-16th century).
identified_threats: Road widening, Missing stones at plinths, Erosion
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019.
